When kvm_mmu_get_page() gets a page with unsynced children
pagetable is unsynchronized with the guest pagetable. But the
guest might not issue a ""flush"" operation on it when the pagetable
entry is changed from zero or other cases. The hypervisor has the
responsibility to synchronize the pagetables.
KVM behaved as above for many years
(""KVM: x86/mmu: Use KVM_REQ_TLB_FLUSH_CURRENT for MMU specific flushes"")
inadvertently included a line of code to change it without giving any
reason in the changelog. It is clear that the commit's intention was to
change KVM_REQ_TLB_FLUSH -> KVM_REQ_TLB_FLUSH_CURRENT
needlessly flush other contexts; however
a nearby KVM_REQ_MMU_SYNC instead.  This patch changes it back.
